newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae meets EPS estimates as charge-offs fall.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae meets EPS estimates as charge-offs fall.

text.p: Fannie Mae said Thursday it is well-positioned for the future at a time when investors are expressing uncertainty about whether corporate earnings expectations can be met.

First Call estimates for Fannie Mae's first quarter were $0.67 per share, which the company met when it announced earnings earlier today. The company said it had accomplished its results by growth in each revenue category and only a modest rise in total expenses.
Fannie Mae said loan charge-offs fell by $17.2 million during the first quarter, enabling it to reduce its provision for losses by $10.0 million while adding further to its loan loss reserves.

The company also said that charge-offs declined to $31.2 million in the first quarter from $48.4 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 as a result of reductions in both single-family and multifamily charge-offs.
